questions.question_text: What is the mechanical process of spinning in textile production?
options: A) Washing clothes in hot soapy water
B) Drawing out and continuously twisting loose raw fibers together to form strong thread or yarn
C) Cutting woven cloth into shirt shapes
D) Dyeing threads in boiling color tubs
questions.correct_answer: B) Drawing out and continuously twisting loose raw fibers together to form strong thread or yarn
questions.detailed_explanation: Spinning draws out and twists loose fibers (using spindles or charkhas) to interlock fibers into yarn.

questions.question_text: In woven fabric, stationary vertical threads are called warp threads, while horizontal threads woven across them are called _____ threads.
questions.correct_answer: weft
questions.detailed_explanation: Warp threads run vertically; weft threads interlace horizontally over and under warp threads at right angles.

questions.question_text: Which animal produces the ultra-soft undercoat fleece used to weave Pashmina shawls?
options: A) Merino sheep
B) Changthangi goat
C) Bactrian camel
D) Angora rabbit
questions.correct_answer: B) Changthangi goat
questions.detailed_explanation: Pashmina wool is harvested from Changthangi goats raised in high-altitude cold deserts of Ladakh.

questions.question_text: Hand-spun and hand-woven cotton cloth championed by Mahatma Gandhi is called _____.
questions.correct_answer: Khadi
questions.detailed_explanation: Khadi is hand-spun cotton fabric made on a charkha, symbolizing self-reliance (*Atmanirbhar*).

questions.question_text: Which tool was traditionally used in Indian households to spin raw cotton into yarn?
options: A) Charkha
B) Handloom
C) Sewing needle
D) Scissors
questions.correct_answer: A) Charkha
questions.detailed_explanation: The charkha is a traditional spinning wheel used to twist raw fibers into continuous cotton thread.

questions.question_text: Silk threads are unwound from protective _____ spun by silkworm caterpillars.
questions.correct_answer: cocoons
questions.detailed_explanation: Silkworm caterpillars spin protein cocoons around themselves, which are unwound into raw silk thread.

questions.question_text: Where does Pashmina wool come from, and how is it harvested without harming the animal?
questions.correct_answer: Pashmina comes from the fine undercoat fleece of Changthangi goats raised in cold Ladakh. It is combed out gently by hand during spring shedding.
questions.detailed_explanation: Nomadic Changpa herders comb out the fine winter undercoat shed naturally by Changthangi goats in high-altitude cold deserts.

questions.question_text: Why did Mahatma Gandhi champion hand-spun Khadi cloth made on a charkha during India's freedom movement?
options: A) Because machine-made cloth was too colorful.
B) To promote national economic self-reliance (Atmanirbhar), boycott foreign factory cloth, and empower rural spinners.
C) Charkhas generated solar electricity for villages.
D) Khadi was mandatory for sports games.
questions.correct_answer: B) To promote national economic self-reliance (Atmanirbhar), boycott foreign factory cloth, and empower rural spinners.
questions.detailed_explanation: Khadi represented economic self-reliance (Atmanirbhar) and political resistance against colonial economic exploitation.

questions.question_text: What is the key structural difference between spinning and weaving?
options: A) Spinning converts loose fibers into thread by twisting; weaving interlaces threads at right angles into fabric.
B) Spinning uses needles; weaving uses soap.
C) Spinning cuts cloth; weaving dyes threads.
D) There is no difference.
questions.correct_answer: A) Spinning converts loose fibers into thread by twisting; weaving interlaces threads at right angles into fabric.
questions.detailed_explanation: Spinning produces thread from raw fibers; weaving interlaces perpendicular threads (warp and weft) to form cloth.

questions.question_text: Give two examples of natural fibers derived from plants and two from animals.
questions.correct_answer: Plant fibers: Cotton, Jute. Animal fibers: Silk (cocoons), Wool (sheep/goat fleece).
questions.detailed_explanation: Plant fibers come from bolls/stems; animal fibers come from protective fleeces or insect silk cocoons.

questions.question_text: Which nomadic community raises Changthangi goats in the high-altitude cold deserts of Ladakh?
options: A) Bakarwals
B) Changpa nomadic herders
C) Maldharis
D) Gujjars
questions.correct_answer: B) Changpa nomadic herders
questions.detailed_explanation: The Changpa nomadic community raises Changthangi goats in extreme sub-zero Changthang high plateaus of Ladakh.

questions.question_text: Traditional patchwork quilts stitched from old recycled garments in Indian homes are called _____.
questions.correct_answer: gudris (quilts)
questions.detailed_explanation: Gudris are traditional quilts made by layering and hand-stitching old cotton garments together.

questions.question_text: How does the tailorbird demonstrate biological stitching when building its nest?
questions.correct_answer: The tailorbird punctures holes along broad leaf edges with its sharp beak, pulling plant fibers or spider silk through to sew a nest sleeve.
questions.detailed_explanation: Tailorbirds use beak puncture mechanics and flexible fibers to stitch living leaf edges into a protective nest pouch.

questions.question_text: Why do raw cotton fibers pull apart easily, whereas spun cotton thread exhibits high tensile strength?
questions.correct_answer: Single raw fibers are short and smooth. Twisting during spinning forces fibers to wrap tightly around each other, creating lateral friction that prevents slipping.
questions.detailed_explanation: Torsional torque converts individual fiber lengths into an integrated, friction-bound yarn strand.

questions.question_text: How does recycling old clothes into patchwork quilts (gudris) demonstrate environmental sustainability?
options: A) It increases garbage dumping in local rivers.
B) It reuses existing textile fibers, prevents landfill waste, and conserves water and agricultural land needed for new cotton.
C) Old cloth produces electricity when folded.
D) It eliminates the need for washing clothes.
questions.correct_answer: B) It reuses existing textile fibers, prevents landfill waste, and conserves water and agricultural land needed for new cotton.
questions.detailed_explanation: Upcycling extends material life, reducing demand for fresh raw resources and curbing landfill waste.

questions.question_text: Trace the production steps required to turn a silkworm cocoon into silk fabric.
questions.correct_answer: (1) Harvest intact cocoons, (2) Soften cocoon gum in hot water, (3) Unwind fine silk filaments and spin into thread, (4) Weave thread on looms.
questions.detailed_explanation: Sericulture processes silk protein filaments from softening cocoons to spinning thread and handloom weaving.

questions.question_text: Why is Pashmina wool significantly warmer than ordinary sheep wool despite being extremely lightweight?
options: A) Changthangi goat undercoat fibers are ultra-fine (12-15 microns), trapping dense microscopic air pockets that insulate against sub-zero cold.
B) Pashmina wool contains active heating chemical elements.
C) Pashmina is heavy like lead.
D) Pashmina absorbs heat from water.
questions.correct_answer: A) Changthangi goat undercoat fibers are ultra-fine (12-15 microns), trapping dense microscopic air pockets that insulate against sub-zero cold.
questions.detailed_explanation: Microscopic fiber fineness traps stagnant air pockets, providing exceptional thermal insulation per unit mass.

questions.question_text: Torsional twisting during spinning generates lateral _____ that holds short cotton fibers together as strong yarn.
questions.correct_answer: friction
questions.detailed_explanation: Frictional binding between twisted fiber surfaces prevents slippage under tension.

questions.question_text: Contrast handloom Khadi weaving with industrial powerloom textile manufacturing in terms of energy use and employment.
questions.correct_answer: Handloom Khadi operates manually with human muscle power (zero grid electricity) and creates widespread rural employment, whereas powerlooms consume heavy electricity and reduce labor.
questions.detailed_explanation: Handloom Khadi represents zero-carbon sustainable manufacturing and rural livelihood support.

questions.question_text: Which environmental hazard is reduced when synthetic polyester clothing purchases are minimized?
options: A) Microplastic pollution in oceans and non-biodegradable synthetic textile landfill waste
B) Increased forest growth
C) Reduced rainfall
D) Depletion of mountain glaciers
questions.correct_answer: A) Microplastic pollution in oceans and non-biodegradable synthetic textile landfill waste
questions.detailed_explanation: Synthetic fibers (nylon/polyester) release persistent microplastics during washing and accumulate indefinitely in landfills.
